related_questions.question: What is the best thing to take for COVID-19?

text_blocks.snippet: For mild COVID-19, symptom relief can be achieved with over-the-counter medications like acetaminophen or ibuprofen. Rest, hydration, and monitoring symptoms are also crucial. High-risk individuals may be eligible for prescription medications to prevent severe illness.

list.snippet: Fever reducers/pain relievers: Acetaminophen (Tylenol) or ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin) can help manage fever and body aches.
Cough suppressants: Cough syrups or medications can help relieve coughing fits.
Other symptom relief: Nasal decongestants or throat lozenges may also be helpful depending on the symptoms.
Individuals at high risk of severe COVID-19 illness may be eligible for prescription antiviral medications like Paxlovid. These medications can help prevent mild illness from worsening.
High-risk individuals include those 65 and older, those with certain medical conditions, and those with weakened immune systems.
Rest and Hydration: Resting and drinking plenty of fluids are essential for recovery.
Monitoring Symptoms: If symptoms worsen or become severe, seek medical advice.
Isolation: If you have COVID-19, isolate yourself from others to prevent spreading the virus.
Consult your doctor: Consult with a healthcare professional for personalized advice on managing COVID-19.

related_questions.question: What are the psychiatric symptoms of Covid-19?

text_blocks.snippet: COVID-19 can lead to a range of neuropsychiatric symptoms, including sleep disturbances, fatigue, cognitive impairment, anxiety, and post-traumatic stress. These symptoms can persist for months after the initial infection and may be more prevalent in individuals with severe COVID-19.
snippet_highlighted_words: sleep disturbances, fatigue, cognitive impairment, anxiety, and post-traumatic stress

list.snippet: Sleep Disturbances: Insomnia and other sleep problems are frequently reported.
Fatigue: Persistent tiredness and low energy are common.
Cognitive Impairment: Difficulty with memory, concentration, and other cognitive functions.
Anxiety: Increased anxiety levels and anxiety disorders.
Post-Traumatic Stress: Symptoms related to the traumatic experience of being ill with COVID-19.
Depression: Some individuals experience depressive symptoms.

list.title: Severity of Infection:
list.snippet: Individuals with more severe COVID-19 cases may experience more pronounced neuropsychiatric symptoms.

list.title: Duration of Infection:
list.snippet: The longer the infection persists, the higher the likelihood of developing neuropsychiatric issues.

list.title: Individual Susceptibility:
list.snippet: Some individuals may be more prone to developing these symptoms due to pre-existing conditions or other factors.

list.title: Interdisciplinary Approach:
list.snippet: Treatment may involve a combination of medication, therapy, and other non-drug therapies.

list.title: Antidepressants:
list.snippet: Antidepressant medications can be helpful for managing depressive symptoms.

list.title: Therapy:
list.snippet: Psychotherapy can help individuals cope with anxiety, depression, and other mental health challenges.

list.title: Other Therapies:
list.snippet: Visual art, music, and physical therapy can also be beneficial.

related_questions.question: What do I do if I've been exposed to someone who tested positive for COVID-19?

text_blocks.snippet: If you've been exposed to someone who tested positive for COVID-19, you should immediately start taking precautions, including wearing a high-quality mask, avoiding places where you can't wear a mask, and taking extra precautions around vulnerable individuals. You should also get tested at least 5 days after your last exposure, even if you don't have symptoms, and continue taking precautions through day 10.
snippet_highlighted_words: immediately start taking precautions, including wearing a high-quality mask, avoiding places where you can't wear a mask, and taking extra precautions around vulnerable individuals

list.snippet: Start Precautions Immediately: Begin taking precautions right away, even before you get tested.
High-Quality Mask: Wear a high-quality mask or respirator, such as an N95, whenever you're around others.
Avoid Crowds: Avoid crowded indoor spaces where you can't wear a mask consistently.
Vulnerable Individuals: Be extra careful around people who are more likely to get very sick from COVID-19.
Testing: Get tested for COVID-19 at least 5 full days after your last exposure.
Monitor Symptoms: Watch for any symptoms of COVID-19.
Isolation: If you test positive, isolate yourself at home according to guidance from your healthcare provider or local health department.
